title: Pumpkin purée
method: Peel the pumpkin, scrape out the seeds, and cut the flesh into chunks.
Steam for about 15 minutes, or bake at 200°C for about 25 minutes, until very soft.
Blend with a spoon of breast milk, formula, or water until smooth.
Cool until just warm.
Do not add salt or sugar.
issues: Salt or sugar is sometimes stirred into pumpkin, and a six-month-old does not need either.
changes: No change is needed beyond keeping salt and sugar out.
Bake or steam the pumpkin and loosen it with breast milk, formula, or water.
serve: Offer a few teaspoons on a spoon, and thin it if it sits too thick.

title: Peach purée

ingredients.note: only if the blend is too thick

method: Cut the fruit off the stone and discard every piece of stone.
Peel the fruit and cut away any bruised parts.
Steam for about 8 minutes, until soft.
Blend until smooth, with a spoon of water only if you need it.
Look through the purée again for any stone fragment.
Do not add sugar.
issues: A piece of stone left in the fruit is a choking hazard.
Unripe fruit will not blend to a smooth first purée.
changes: Use ripe peach or apricot, peel it, and take the stone out completely.
Steam and blend until smooth, with no sugar.
serve: Serve warm or cool on a spoon, after one more look for stone fragments.

title: Potato purée

ingredients.item: cooking water, breast milk, or formula
ingredients.note: or the same amount of pasteurised full-fat cow's milk, which is a milk allergen

method: Peel the potatoes and cut them into even chunks.
Boil in water until a knife slides through, with no salt in the pot.
Drain, and keep some of the cooking water.
Mash with cooking water, breast milk, or formula until smooth.
Use pasteurised full-fat cow's milk only if you accept the milk allergen.
Do not add salt.
issues: Potato is low in iron, so a bowl of it is a poor meal on its own.
Cow's milk adds a milk allergen, and salt is often mashed in.
changes: Mash with cooking water, breast milk, or formula, and use pasteurised full-fat cow's milk only if that allergen is already the plan.
Do not add salt, and serve the purée with meat, lentils, or a fully cooked egg.
serve: Pair it with meat, lentils, or a fully cooked egg so the plate supplies iron. Cooking water, breast milk, or formula keeps cow's milk out.

title: Apple purée

ingredients.note: for the pan, plus a spoon more if the blend is thick

method: Peel the apples, cut out the cores, and slice the flesh.
Cook in a small splash of water until completely soft, about 10 minutes.
Blend until smooth.
Cool until just warm.
Do not add sugar.
issues: Raw grated apple is a poor first texture.
Sugar is often added, and the apple does not need it.
changes: Cook the apple until soft and blend it smooth, with no sugar.
Save raw grated apple until the baby is chewing well.
serve: Serve the cooked purée on a spoon. Raw grated apple waits until chewing is reliable.

title: Pear purée
method: Peel the pears and remove the cores.
Cook in a small splash of water until soft, about 8 minutes.
Blend until smooth.
Cool until just warm.
Do not add sugar.
issues: The skin and core do not belong in a first purée, and sugar is unnecessary.
changes: Peel the ripe pear, remove the core, cook, and blend.
No other change is needed if salt and sugar stay out.
serve: Serve warm or cool, smooth enough for a spoon.

title: Sweet potato purée
method: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Prick the sweet potatoes and bake until the flesh is very soft, about 40 minutes.
Cool enough to handle, then scoop the flesh out of the skins.
Mash or blend until smooth, with a spoon of water or breast milk if it is stiff.
Do not add salt or sugar.
issues: This is a strong first food, and the usual mistake is seasoning it.
changes: Bake, scoop, and loosen the flesh.
Keep salt and sugar out, and nothing else needs to change.
serve: A few teaspoons is a full first taste. The flavour is already sweet.

title: Mango purée

ingredients.note: flesh only, peeled and cut off the stone

method: Choose a ripe mango that gives slightly when pressed.
Peel it and cut the flesh off the stone.
Trim away stringy fibre.
Blend until smooth.
Do not cook it, and do not add sugar.
issues: Mango purée is slippery, and thick pieces slide off a spoon.
Cooking a ripe mango is unnecessary.
changes: Blend ripe mango and serve it on a spoon.
A ripe mango needs no cooking and no sugar.
serve: Serve on a spoon so it does not slide. A few teaspoons is enough for a first taste.

title: Banana mash
method: Peel a ripe banana.
Mash it with a fork until completely smooth.
Serve half now and keep the other half covered for the next meal the same day.
Do not add sugar, and do not offer this as the meal every day.
issues: Banana is low in iron, so it is a poor everyday staple.
A lot of banana can slow the bowels.
changes: Mash a ripe banana and offer a small portion now and then, not as the main food each day.
Keep meat, lentils, or egg in other meals so iron is not missed.
serve: Offer a small mash, not a banana at every meal. Put an iron-rich food on the table the same day.

title: Apple and chestnut purée

ingredients.note: plain, with no sugar and no salt, not a sweetened spread
prepared weight, peeled, cored, and cooked until soft

method: Use plain cooked chestnuts that are fully peeled, or boil peeled chestnuts until soft.
Cook the peeled, cored apple until soft.
Blend chestnut and apple together until there are no pieces left.
Add a spoon of cooking water only if the blade stalls.
Do not add sugar.
issues: Chestnut pieces can choke if the purée is not fully smooth.
Chestnut allergy exists, and chestnut is not the same food as peanut or walnut.
changes: Blend cooked peeled chestnut with cooked apple until completely smooth, and give a small first portion on a day when the baby is well.
Do not count this as the tree-nut introduction, and do not use a sweetened chestnut spread.
serve: Keep it completely smooth. Start with a small portion on a well day.

title: Blueberry and apple purée

ingredients.note: fresh or frozen, with no added sugar

method: Peel and core the apple and cut it into slices.
Cook the apple with the blueberries and a splash of water until the apple is soft.
Squash the berries so the skins burst.
Blend until smooth.
Do not add sugar.
issues: Whole blueberry skins are a poor texture in a first purée.
changes: Cook the apple and squash the blueberries so the skins burst, then blend smooth.
No sugar is needed.
serve: Serve on a spoon. The colour will stain, which is harmless.

title: Avocado and banana purée
method: Halve the avocado and lift out the stone.
Scoop the flesh and mash it with a fork.
Mash in half a ripe banana until smooth.
Serve straight away, before the surface browns.
Do not add salt or sugar.
issues: Avocado browns quickly and is best eaten at once.
changes: Mash ripe avocado with a little banana and serve it straight away.
The fats are useful, and no salt is needed.
serve: Serve straight away. A few teaspoons gives useful fat without a large banana portion.

title: More purée mixes

ingredients.note: cooked weight, peeled and pitted where needed
cooked weight; a third food, if you add one, stays the smallest part
only for the pear and yogurt pair; this is a milk allergen

method: Choose two foods the baby already eats, or three at most.
Cook them until soft, peel and pit as needed, and blend with a spoon of cooking water until smooth.
Use pairs such as pumpkin and apple, broccoli and potato, and pea and sweet potato.
Other sound pairs are zucchini and carrot, pear and plain yogurt, and chicken and pumpkin.
Cook chicken through with no pink, and cook any vegetable until it mashes easily.
There is no need to wait months between ordinary vegetables, and the yogurt pair is the one with a milk allergen.
issues: Families sometimes wait months between ordinary vegetables for no nutritional reason.
Yogurt, if you use that pair, is a milk allergen.
changes: Cook and mix two familiar foods, three at most, once each has been eaten on its own.
Ordinary vegetables do not need months between them, and only the pear and yogurt pair contains milk.
serve: One mix on a well day is enough. Freeze the vegetable and meat mixes; eat the yogurt pair the same day.

title: Apple and peach semolina with yogurt

ingredients.note: alongside; lentils boiled until completely soft

method: Stir the semolina into boiling water and cook, stirring, until soft and thick.
Cook peeled apple and pitted peeled peach until soft, and blend them smooth.
Cool the semolina until warm, then stir in the yogurt, fruit, and a pinch of Ceylon cinnamon if you want it.
Do not add biscuit crumbs or sugar.
Serve with shredded chicken cooked through, or with lentils boiled until completely soft.
issues: Semolina is low in iron, so it should not be the whole meal.
Biscuit crumbs add little of use and more gluten.
changes: Cook the semolina in water, then stir in plain full-fat yogurt and cooked apple and peach, with a pinch of Ceylon cinnamon if you want it.
Add shredded chicken or well-cooked lentils alongside, and leave biscuit crumbs out.
serve: Serve warm, with chicken or lentils so the bowl is not only semolina. This contains milk and gluten.

title: Pear and banana with oats
method: Peel and core the pear and cook it in a splash of water until soft.
Stir the oats into the water and cook until soft and smooth, about 5 minutes.
Mash the banana and stir it into the warm oats with the pear.
Blend until smooth.
Do not add biscuit crumbs or sugar.
issues: The usual topping is a sweet shop biscuit, which this bowl does not need.
Oats count as gluten here.
changes: Use fine oats cooked soft with pear and banana, instead of biscuit crumbs.
Leave the sweet crumb topping out.
serve: Serve warm and smooth. This is the biscuit-free version, and it contains gluten.

title: Plum and peach with yogurt
method: Cut the plum and peach flesh off the stones and throw the stones away.
Peel the fruit.
Steam until soft, about 8 minutes, then blend smooth.
Cool until warm and stir into the yogurt.
Run a spoon through to catch any bit of stone.
Do not add sugar.
issues: The stones are the hazard.
Flavoured yogurt often contains added sugar.
changes: Pit and peel the plum and peach, cook and blend them, and stir them into plain pasteurised full-fat yogurt.
No other change is needed.
serve: Stir and serve the same day. This contains milk.

title: Green apple and blueberry with curd

ingredients.note: fresh or frozen, no added sugar

ingredients.item: pasteurised full-fat curd or cottage cheese
ingredients.note: no added salt if you can find it; milk allergen

method: Peel, core, and cook the apple with the blueberries until soft.
Squash the berries so the skins burst, then blend the fruit smooth.
Stir the yogurt into the curd until it loosens.
Fold the warm fruit into the curd.
Do not add biscuit crumbs or sugar.
issues: This is often held back until 9 or 10 months for no nutritional reason.
Biscuit crumbs are commonly added and are not needed.
changes: Serve it from 6 months, with cooked apple and blueberry stirred into pasteurised curd loosened with yogurt.
Leave the biscuit out.
serve: Serve from six months, the same day. This contains milk.

title: Pineapple with curd

ingredients.note: fresh flesh, core removed, not canned in syrup

ingredients.item: pasteurised full-fat curd or cottage cheese
ingredients.note: no added salt if you can find it; milk allergen

method: Cut the core and skin off a very ripe pineapple and take a small piece of flesh.
Chop that flesh very fine, with no fibrous threads.
Stir the yogurt into the curd.
Fold the pineapple through the curd.
Do not add sugar, and do not offer this as a first purée.
issues: Pineapple can sting a baby's mouth, so this is not a first purée.
It is often delayed until 11 months without a good reason.
changes: Use only a small amount of very ripe pineapple, chopped very fine, folded into curd and yogurt.
Age 8 is enough, so do not wait until 11 months.
serve: A small bowl from eight months. Stop if it stings, and try less another week. This contains milk.

title: Apple and yogurt oat porridge

ingredients.note: peeled, cored, and cooked, with no sugar

method: Peel, core, and cook the apple until soft, then mash it smooth.
Stir the oats into the water and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Cool the porridge until warm.
Stir in the yogurt and the apple.
Do not add sugar.
issues: The older version of this dish used rhubarb, which is harsh and high in oxalate.
Rhubarb usually needs sugar, which does not belong in this bowl.
changes: Drop the rhubarb, and stir plain yogurt into warm oat porridge and cooked apple instead.
The bowl still contains milk and gluten from the yogurt and the oats.
serve: Serve the porridge warm with the yogurt stirred in. Do not put rhubarb in this bowl.

title: Spinach and potato

ingredients.note: washed leaves, a small share of the bowl
peeled cored pear, or peas, for vitamin C
not water from a private well

method: Peel the potatoes and boil them in tap water until soft.
Add the spinach for the last 2 minutes, until wilted.
Stir in cooked pear or peas.
Drain, keeping a spoon of the tap cooking water, and blend until smooth.
Do not cook this in water from a private well, and do not add salt.
issues: The usual green stew relied on sorrel, or on spinach as the whole dish.
Sorrel is a poor everyday green for infants because it is high in oxalate.
changes: Make a potato and spinach mash with cooked pear or peas for vitamin C, and keep spinach as one part of the meal rather than the only vegetable.
Do not cook it in water from a private well, which can be high in nitrate, and do not use sorrel.
serve: Serve as a mixed bowl, not a plate of spinach alone. Use tap water, not water from a private well.

title: White bean purée

ingredients.note: or 240 g unsalted canned beans, rinsed

method: If using dried beans, soak them, drain them, and boil in fresh water at a rolling boil until completely soft, often 45 to 90 minutes, with no firm centre.
If using canned beans, choose unsalted ones, rinse them, and heat them through.
Peel the carrot and cook it until soft.
Blend beans and carrot with a little cooking water until smooth.
Stir in the olive oil.
Do not add salt.
issues: Undercooked dried beans can make a child ill.
Canned beans are often salted.
changes: Boil dried beans hard until they are completely soft, or rinse unsalted canned beans and heat them.
Blend with cooked carrot and olive oil, and do not add salt.
serve: Blend until smooth. There should be no firm core in a bean.

title: Asparagus and potato with cheese

ingredients.note: tender part only, woody ends snapped off
a small handful grated, shared across all 4 portions; milk allergen

method: Peel the potatoes and cut them into chunks.
Snap the woody ends off the asparagus and use the tender part.
Boil potatoes and asparagus in unsalted water until the stalks squash easily.
Drain, keeping a spoon of cooking water.
Add the grated cheese and blend until smooth.
Do not add more cheese, and do not add salt.
issues: Asparagus stays fibrous if it is not cooked very soft.
Cheese is salty, so a large amount is too much sodium at this age.
changes: Cook new potato and asparagus until the stalks squash easily, then blend.
Use only a small handful of pasteurised mild cheese grated across 4 portions.
serve: All 4 portions share 30 g of cheese. Serve warm. This contains milk.

title: Zucchini and potato purée

ingredients.note: white and pale green only, root and outer layer removed

method: Peel the zucchini and the potato, and slice the washed leek.
Cook all three in a little unsalted water until very soft.
Blend with a spoon of cooking water until smooth.
Stir in the olive oil.
Do not add salt.
issues: This is often held to 9 months for no good reason.
Salt is sometimes added to the leek and potato.
changes: Offer the blended zucchini, potato, and leek from 6 months.
Finish with olive oil and leave the salt out.
serve: Serve from six months, smooth, with no salt.

title: Carrot and Jerusalem artichoke

ingredients.note: a small piece only, peeled, because more can cause gas

method: Peel the carrots and the small piece of Jerusalem artichoke.
Cut them into chunks and boil in unsalted water until very soft.
Blend until smooth, with a spoon of cooking water if needed.
Stir in the olive oil at the end.
Do not add a stock cube or salt.
issues: Jerusalem artichoke can cause painful gas if the portion is large.
A stock cube is salty and does not belong in the pot.
changes: Use mostly carrot and only a small piece of Jerusalem artichoke.
Stir in olive oil at the end, start at 8 months, and do not use a stock cube.
serve: Start at eight months with a small serving. The artichoke is only a small part of the bowl.

title: Cauliflower and broccoli with cheese

ingredients.note: florets, tough stalk peeled if you use it
modest amount; skip it for the milk-free path
use this instead of cheese if you want the dish milk-free

method: Cut the broccoli and cauliflower into small florets.
Steam or boil in unsalted water until very soft.
Blend with a spoon of cooking water until smooth.
Stir in the grated cheese while the purée is warm, and blend again.
For a milk-free bowl, skip the cheese and stir in the olive oil instead.
Do not add salt, and do not increase the cheese.
issues: Cheese is salty if the amount is more than modest.
A baby who needs a milk-free plate cannot eat the cheese version.
changes: Blend broccoli and cauliflower with a little pasteurised cheese, or with olive oil if you want it milk-free.
Keep the cheese modest, and no other change is needed.
serve: The cheese version contains milk. The olive oil version does not. Keep the cheese to 30 g across 4 portions.

title: Fish with sweet potato and celeriac

ingredients.note: fresh or plain frozen, not smoked; not carp
or a few fresh leaves, stem removed

method: Peel the sweet potato and celeriac and cook them in unsalted water until soft.
Add the fish and thyme and simmer until the fish is opaque and flakes, about 5 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and check the fish with clean fingers, removing every bone.
Blend until smooth.
Do not add salt, and do not use carp.
issues: Celeriac is a celery allergen.
Carp is a poor choice because of the bones.
changes: Use boneless salmon, trout, cod, or hake, cooked through, and check for bones.
Blend it with sweet potato, celeriac, and thyme, and do not use carp.
serve: Check for bones again on the plate. This contains fish and celery.

title: Spring vegetables with cauliflower

ingredients.note: tender part only, cooked very soft

method: Peel the potato and zucchini, snap woody ends off the asparagus, and chop the cauliflower fine.
Cook potato, zucchini, asparagus, and cauliflower in unsalted water until very soft.
Add the peas and cook until they squash easily.
Blend until smooth.
Do not add a stock cube or salt.
Leave cheese out; a teaspoon of it would add a milk allergen, and the base has none.
issues: Salty stock is often used and is not needed.
The same plate is sometimes delayed until 10 months for no good reason.
changes: Cook potato, pea, zucchini, and very soft asparagus, with cauliflower chopped fine, and use no stock.
Serve from 6 months, and add cheese only as an option because a teaspoon would bring in a milk allergen the base does not have.
serve: Serve from six months with no stock. Add cheese only if milk is already accepted, and then it becomes a milk allergen.

title: Chestnut, apple, and chicken

ingredients.note: plain, no sugar and no salt
prepared weight, peeled, cored, and cooked

method: Cook the chicken in unsalted water until there is no pink in the middle.
Cook the peeled, cored apple until soft.
Use plain cooked peeled chestnuts, not a sweetened spread.
Blend chicken, apple, and chestnut until completely smooth, with a spoon of cooking water if needed.
Check that no chestnut piece remains.
Do not add salt.
issues: Chestnut must be smooth, because pieces can choke.
Fruit alone would miss the iron that the chicken supplies.
changes: Blend cooked chestnut, cooked apple, and fully cooked chicken until smooth.
This is a better plate than fruit alone, and no salt is added.
serve: Serve a smooth spoonful. The chicken is there for iron, and the chestnut must have no pieces.

title: Tomato vegetable pasta

ingredients.note: fresh, peeled, not a salted sauce

method: Peel the carrot, zucchini, and tomatoes and chop them small.
Cook the vegetables in a splash of unsalted water until very soft, then mash them.
Boil the pasta in unsalted water well past the usual timing, until it is very soft.
Drain the pasta and mash it into the sauce so no firm piece remains.
Do not add salt, and do not wait for an older month to serve it.
issues: Pasta that is still firm is too hard at 6 months.
An older month is sometimes printed on this dish for no good reason.
changes: Cook small pasta until very soft and mash it into a no-salt tomato, carrot, and zucchini sauce.
Do not wait for a later month, since the pasta is only a gluten food served very soft.
serve: Mash the pasta so nothing firm is left. Serve from six months. This contains gluten.

title: Zucchini, pea, salmon, and couscous

ingredients.note: fresh or plain frozen, not smoked

method: Peel and cook the zucchini, and cook the peas until they squash easily.
Cook the salmon until it is opaque and flakes, then cool it enough to handle.
Flake the salmon and remove every bone.
Stir the couscous into the hot water, cover for 5 minutes, then mash it with a little extra water so no dry grains remain.
Smash the peas and mash salmon, zucchini, and couscous together until spoonable.
Do not add salt.
issues: Couscous is wheat, so this contains gluten.
Whole peas and a leftover fish bone are the texture hazards.
changes: Smash the peas, and flake boneless salmon only after the bones are checked.
Stir them into soft couscous with cooked zucchini.
serve: Look through the salmon for bones, and smash every pea. This contains gluten and fish.

title: Yellow fish purée

ingredients.note: fresh or plain frozen, not smoked

method: Peel the sweet potato and carrot and cook them in unsalted water until soft.
Add the fish and cook until it is opaque and flakes.
Check the fish and remove every bone.
Blend fish and vegetables until smooth.
Do not add salt or nutmeg.
issues: The usual version salted the fish and added nutmeg.
A bone left in the purée is dangerous.
changes: Cook boneless fish with sweet potato and carrot, check for bones, and blend it smooth.
Do not add salt, and skip the nutmeg.
serve: No salt and no nutmeg. Check the fish for bones before you blend. This contains fish.

title: Pea, sweet potato, and fish

ingredients.note: fresh or frozen, to be smashed
fresh or plain frozen, not smoked

method: Peel the sweet potato and cook it in unsalted water until soft.
Add the peas and cook until they squash easily.
Add the fish and cook until it is opaque and flakes.
Remove every bone.
Smash the peas and blend everything until smooth.
Do not add salt.
issues: Whole peas are a poor texture in a first purée.
A label of 7 or 8 months is later than this dish needs.
changes: Smash the peas and blend them with sweet potato and boneless white fish, after the bones are checked.
Serve it from 6 months rather than from 7 or 8 months.
serve: Serve from six months. Smash the peas and check the fish for bones. This contains fish.

title: Aubergine and chicken
method: Peel the aubergine and the potato and cut them into chunks.
Put them in a pan with the chicken and enough unsalted water to cover.
Cook until the chicken has no pink in the middle and the aubergine is soft and mild.
Blend until smooth, with a spoon of cooking water if needed.
Do not salt the aubergine first.
issues: Aubergine can taste bitter if the skin is left on and it is undercooked.
Salting the aubergine is a common step and adds sodium a baby does not need.
changes: Peel the aubergine and cook it with potato and chicken until very soft, then blend.
Do not salt the aubergine.
serve: Peel it and cook it until soft and mild. Do not salt it first.

title: Chicken and apple with couscous

ingredients.note: prepared weight, peeled, cored, and cooked; a flavour, not the bulk

method: Cook the chicken in unsalted water until there is no pink in the middle, then shred it very fine.
Peel, core, and cook the apple until soft, then mash it.
Stir the couscous into hot water, not stock, and cover for 5 minutes.
Mash the couscous with a spoon of water so no dry grains remain.
Mix chicken, apple, and couscous and mash until spoonable.
Do not add cherries or salt.
issues: Whole cherries are a choking hazard and do not belong in this dish.
Salty stock is often used to cook the couscous.
changes: Use cooked apple only as a flavour, and keep the chicken as the iron-rich part.
Cook the couscous in water rather than stock, and count the gluten from the wheat.
serve: The apple is only a flavour and the chicken is the iron. No cherries and no stock. This contains gluten.

title: Broccoli, sweet potato, and chicken

ingredients.note: about 1 tsp in each portion, stirred in at the end

method: Peel the sweet potato and cut it into chunks.
Cook it with the chicken in unsalted water until the chicken has no pink and the sweet potato is soft.
Add the broccoli and cook until very soft.
Blend until smooth.
Stir in the oil.
Do not add salt.
issues: This is a sound first meal, and the usual gap is leaving the fat out.
changes: Blend broccoli, sweet potato, and fully cooked chicken, then stir in a teaspoon of rapeseed or olive oil on each portion.
Do not add salt, and nothing else needs to change.
serve: This is a sound first meal. Each portion gets about a teaspoon of oil.

title: White vegetable pasta
method: Peel the potato and cook it with the cauliflower in unsalted water until very soft.
Stir in the parsley and mash the vegetables smooth.
Boil the pasta in unsalted water until it is very soft, well past firm.
Drain and mash the pasta into the vegetable mash.
Do not add salt.
issues: Salt is easy to add to a pale pasta dish and is not needed.
Firm pasta is the wrong texture at this age.
changes: Cook the pasta until very soft and mix it with a mash of potato, cauliflower, and parsley.
Leave the salt out, and no other change is needed.
serve: Serve very soft pasta in the pale mash, with no salt. This contains gluten.

title: Veal with vegetables

ingredients.note: lean, raw weight; either meat is a sound choice

method: Cut the meat, peeled carrot, peeled tomato, and onion into small pieces.
Cover with unsalted water and cook until the meat is fully done and the vegetables are soft.
Check there is no pink in the middle of the meat.
Blend until smooth, with a little cooking water if needed.
Do not add salt.
issues: Veal is sometimes treated as a special food, but it is not nutritionally better than beef.
Salt is often added to a meat sauce.
changes: Use beef or veal, since both are equal choices.
Cook the meat with carrot, tomato, and onion until fully done, then blend, and do not add salt.
serve: Beef works the same way as veal. Serve it fully cooked, with no salt. The point of the dish is the iron.

title: Liver and potato with vegetables

ingredients.note: raw weight, so each portion has about 15 g of cooked liver

method: Peel the potato and pumpkin, and peel the tomato.
Cook them in unsalted water until soft.
Add the liver and cook until it is brown all through, with no pink.
Blend until smooth.
Divide so each child's portion contains only about 15 g of the cooked liver.
Do not add salt, and do not serve a second portion in the same week.
issues: Liver is very high in vitamin A, so a large portion or a repeat in the same week is too much.
A vitamin A supplement on top of the liver stacks the dose.
changes: Fully cook the chicken liver, put only about 15 g of cooked liver in the child's portion, and serve liver at most once a week.
Do not pair this meal with a vitamin A supplement.
serve: One portion is the week's liver, about 15 g of cooked liver in that bowl. Freeze the rest for later weeks, and do not also give a vitamin A supplement.

title: Cornmeal and fruit cup

ingredients.note: not whole corn kernels, and not wheat semolina
peeled, cored, and cooked, with no sugar

method: Peel, core, and cook the apple until soft, then mash it.
Whisk the cornmeal into the water.
Cook, stirring, until it is soft and spoonable, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the apple and cool until warm.
Do not add sugar, and do not use whole kernels.
Serve it beside an iron food, not as the only dish.
issues: Cornmeal porridge is low in iron, so it cannot be the whole meal.
Whole corn kernels are the wrong texture, and sugar is sometimes added.
changes: Cook fine cornmeal into a soft porridge with cooked apple, and do not use whole kernels or sugar.
Serve it as a side from 8 months, when a thicker texture is reasonable.
serve: A side from eight months, next to meat, lentils, or egg, not the meal by itself.

title: More mixed plates

ingredients.note: cooked chicken, beef, lentils, or white beans; boil pulses until completely soft
cooked broccoli, carrot, peas, or pumpkin
cooked sweet potato, potato, apple, or pear

method: Put one iron food, one vegetable, and one familiar fruit or starch in the bowl.
Use foods already cooked soft, with meat fully done and any beans or lentils boiled until they have no firm core.
Add a teaspoon of rapeseed or olive oil and blend until smooth.
One plate is chicken, broccoli, and sweet potato.
Another is lentils, carrot, and potato, and a third is beef, peas, and cooked apple.
Finish with white beans, pumpkin, and pear, and do not add salt or a stock cube.
issues: A plate of fruit or starch alone misses iron.
Oil is often forgotten, and salty stock is often used instead.
changes: Build each plate from one iron food, one vegetable, one familiar fruit or starch, and a teaspoon of oil.
Use the four example plates in the method, and do not add salt or stock.
serve: Build one plate this way. The iron food is not optional, and the oil goes on at the end.
